$comment: Patches whose subject is a note: something decides a pitch, something
decides when, and something shapes the sound in between. The oldest and
least glamorous family, and the one most prompts turn out to mean.

idioms.is: An oscillator through a filter through an amplifier, with an envelope opening the amplifier — the standard voice everything else is a variation on.
idioms.sounds_right_when: notes have a clear start and end rather than droning, and the filter audibly removes harmonics.
idioms.source: The east-coast signal chain as set out in Strange

listen_for.sounds_like: a note with a shape: an attack, a body that is duller than the raw waveform, and an ending that the envelope decides rather than the clock
listen_for.confusable_with: a drone with a filter on it, which never stops; the articulation is what separates them

topology.describe: the oscillator has to reach the filter
the filter has to reach the amplifier
an envelope has to open the amplifier, or the voice drones instead of playing notes

common_mistakes.message: nothing opens the amplifier, so the voice drones instead of articulating
the oscillator never reaches the filter, so nothing is subtracted
there is no amplifier, so nothing shapes the loudness

idioms.is: A wavefolded oscillator through a low-pass gate, where one control opens both loudness and brightness together — the west-coast alternative to filter-plus-VCA.
idioms.sounds_right_when: notes are percussive and get duller as they decay, rather than simply quieter.
idioms.source: Patch & Tweak (Bjørn & Meyer), on the low-pass gate

topology.describe: the oscillator has to reach the folder — folding is where west-coast harmonics come from
the folded signal has to reach a gate or amplifier
an envelope has to open it, or the fold sustains rather than plucking

common_mistakes.message: nothing is folded, so this is an east-coast voice wearing the name
nothing opens the gate, so the voice sustains instead of plucking

anchor.quote: a low-pass gate: the combination of a low-pass filter and a VCA

idioms.is: A sequencer supplying both pitch and gate to a voice, so the pattern plays itself in time.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the same phrase repeats in time, with each step clearly articulated.
idioms.source: Standard practice; Strange's chapter on sequential controllers

listen_for.sounds_like: a phrase that repeats exactly, each step separately articulated, landing on the pulse
listen_for.confusable_with: one held note through perfect wiring — which is what a correctly patched sequencer with unwritten steps produces, and the single most common way this patch disappoints

expect.why: the steps are the melody; three or fewer distinct pitches means most of them are still at their default

topology.describe: the sequencer's pitch has to reach the oscillator
the sequencer's gate has to fire an envelope, or every step runs together
the sequencer has to be clocked, or it never advances

common_mistakes.message: the sequencer is never clocked, so it sits on step one
no gate reaches an envelope, so the steps never articulate
the sequence never reaches a pitch input

idioms.is: An oscillator held open through to the output, with no envelope gating it — deliberately continuous.
idioms.sounds_right_when: it never stops and never articulates.

topology.describe: the oscillator has to reach something downstream

common_mistakes.message: the oscillator is not patched into anything

idioms.is: One oscillator modulating another's frequency at audio rate, producing sidebands rather than vibrato.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the timbre is metallic or bell-like and changes character with modulation depth, not just pitch.
idioms.source: Chowning's FM synthesis, as practised in modular form

axis.position: at audio rate, so the movement is heard as timbre
axis.set_by: the modulator's rate, and how much of it reaches the frequency input — both knobs; every position on this axis patches a source to an oscillator's frequency input and they sound nothing alike
axis.$comment: Below hearing this same cable is vibrato; with the depth under an envelope it is an FM voice whose timbre is an event. Three records, one structure, because the difference is rate and amount and this checker reads neither.

topology.describe: one oscillator has to modulate the other's frequency at audio rate
the carrier has to reach an amplifier

common_mistakes.message: neither oscillator modulates the other, so there is no FM
the carrier never reaches an amplifier

idioms.is: A pitch source passed through a quantizer before the oscillator, so whatever voltage arrives lands on a note of the chosen scale.
idioms.sounds_right_when: every note belongs to the scale, however random the source is.
idioms.source: Patch & Tweak (Bjørn & Meyer), on quantizer modules

topology.describe: a pitch source has to reach the quantizer
the quantizer's output has to be what reaches the oscillator — quantizing a voltage nobody uses changes nothing

common_mistakes.message: the oscillator's pitch does not come from the quantizer, so nothing is actually in key
the quantizer has no input

anchor.quote: Quantizer modules auto-correct incoming volt- ages to the nearest1/12volt.

idioms.is: A MIDI or keyboard interface supplying pitch and gate to a voice, so a person plays it rather than the patch playing itself.
idioms.sounds_right_when: nothing happens until a key is pressed.

topology.describe: a pitch source has to reach the oscillator
a gate has to fire the envelope

common_mistakes.message: no gate reaches an envelope, so pressing a key changes nothing
nothing sets the oscillator's pitch

idioms.is: Several oscillators mixed into one filter and amplifier, so a chord is possible but every note shares one envelope.
idioms.sounds_right_when: notes sound together but re-articulate as a group rather than individually.
idioms.source: Standard practice; the honest name for what most modular 'polyphony' is

topology.describe: the oscillators have to be mixed
the mix has to reach the shared filter

common_mistakes.message: the oscillators are never mixed together
the mix never reaches a filter

idioms.is: A low oscillator through a low-pass filter with a fast envelope, kept simple so the low end stays clean.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the note is low and defined rather than muddy, and stops cleanly.

topology.describe: the oscillator has to reach a low-pass filter
an envelope has to shape it, or the bass drones

common_mistakes.message: the bass is never filtered
nothing shapes the bass, so it drones

idioms.is: A harmonically rich source through resonant filters tuned to formant regions, so the timbre reads as a vowel.
idioms.sounds_right_when: you hear a vowel rather than a filter sweep.
idioms.source: Strange's treatment of formant synthesis with resonant filters

listen_for.sounds_like: a vowel — two or three fixed resonant regions that stay put in absolute frequency while the note moves under them
listen_for.confusable_with: a filter sweep, where the resonance follows the note; if the vowel changes when you play higher, the formants are tracking and should not be

topology.describe: a harmonically rich source has to reach the formant filters
the filter bands have to be summed, or only one formant is heard

common_mistakes.message: the formant bands are never summed, so there is no vowel
nothing feeds the formant filters

axis.position: tuned to the formants of a vowel
axis.set_by: where the filters are tuned and how sharp they are — knobs, so the patch that makes a vowel and the patch that makes an instrument body are the same cables
axis.$comment: A bank of parallel band-pass filters summed. Tuned to the vowel formants it reads as a voice; tuned to an instrument's body resonances it reads as that instrument. One structure, and the tuning is what a checker cannot see.

idioms.is: A single sawtooth voice through a steeply resonant low-pass, played by a step sequencer whose pitch passes through a slew so notes slide into one another, with a second sequenced lane opening the cutoff on chosen steps. The slide and the accent are the whole idiom: without them it is an ordinary bassline.
idioms.sounds_right_when: it is a repeating RIFF rather than a wandering line — the ear should be able to sing it back after two passes. Acid lives on a few pitches from ONE minor scale, hammered, with the root repeated often and at least one jump of a full octave (an octave is 1.0 V, a semitone 1/12 V, a fifth 0.583 V). Only some notes slide, so keep the slew time short — a tenth of a step or less — or every note glides and it sounds seasick. The filter is the instrument: resonance high enough to whistle (0.75 of its range or more) and a cutoff that starts LOW, so the accent has somewhere to open to. Keep the envelope's decay a fraction of a step with no sustain, so notes stop before the next begins.
idioms.source: The TB-303's fixed architecture, as used in Chicago acid house

topology.describe: the sequencer's pitch has to pass through a slew — that is the slide
the slewed pitch has to reach the oscillator, not the raw sequencer output
the oscillator has to reach the filter
the filter has to reach the amplifier
an envelope has to articulate each note, or it drones
something sequenced has to open the cutoff on chosen steps — the accent

common_mistakes.message: the sequencer's pitch skips the slew, so no note slides into the next — the sound is a plain bassline
the oscillator takes the raw sequencer output, so the slew is wired to nothing and there is no glide
nothing opens the cutoff on chosen steps, so every note is equally dull and the squelch never happens
no envelope on the amplifier, so the line drones instead of articulating each step
there is no slew in the patch, so the slide the idiom is named for cannot exist
